full_judgment: 5. Mr. Bazlur Rahman Talukder the learned Advocate appearing in support of the rule contends that the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in not relying upon the registered kabala. According to him a registered kabala carries a pre-emption of its genuineness. In the absence of a finding that the kabala was forged the learned Subordinate Judge should have relied upon Ext. 1 and decreed the suit for the reliefs claimed. The contention does not stand the scrutiny of law. The plaintiff cannot succeed on the weakness of the defence case. The plaintiff must prove the facts alleged by him by adducing relevant evidence. P.W.1 was not corroborated by the other witness. P.Ws. 2 and 4 did not support the plaintiff and they were not attesting witnesses to the kabala. The scribe and the attesting witnesses and the identifier were not examined. No reason for their non-examination was disclosed by the plaintiff. In such circumstances, in the absence of proof of due execution of the kabala by the alleged vendor the registered kabala by itself does not raise any presumption of genuineness and the learned Subordinate Judge appears to have correctly refused to rely upon Ext. 1 the kabala which is the foundation of the plaintiff's claim. Further the plaintiff did not claim any relief for declaration of his title on the basis of the kabala. In such circumstances the contention of Mr. Talukder does not stand.
